transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~46m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Derek (CTO, OrchidAI), Priya (Head of Compliance), Luis (SRE), Nora (Product), Jamal (Legal)

[00:00] Samira: Okay everyone, thanks for joining the weekly security pulse for the pilot. Quick check — is this still the right agenda? SSO walkthrough, audit logs & retention, SOC2 artifacts, then open q's.
[00:18] Derek: Yep that sounds right. We've got a couple of people on teams that might chime in.
[00:25] Priya: hi, thanks. We'll want to focus on retention and data deletion more than performance today, but would like a short overview of the logs you collect.
[00:35] Ethan: great, i'll start with the log overview — apologies if the transcript mangles some field names, i'll try to spell them out.

--- Topics: SSO/SAML, Audit logs format, Data retention & deletion, SOC2 evidence, KMS and key rotation ---

[01:10] Ethan: So for the pilot we're exporting audit events at three layers: control-plane events (who created jobs, rollouts), serving events (model variant, tokens, latency buckets), and admin events (role changes, SSO events). The output is JSON lines, timestamped in UTC. Common fields: event_type, user_id, principal_type, resource, action, request_id, latency_ms, bytes_in, bytes_out.
[01:42] Luis: can you show an example? we prefer the columns to be consistent for our log parser. sometimes these fields change between releases.
[01:50] Ethan: yah — sample we'll share after the call — it's pretty stable but there is a slight difference between hosted and dedicated variants in the resource naming (we call them model-shim IDs). i'll include a mapping.
[02:10] Priya: how long do you keep logs by default for hosted pilot? what's the retention window?
[02:15] Samira: default 90 days for hosted, but for pilots we can do shorter or longer — we log to an internal retention tier. For Redwood Dedicated you can set retention at the cluster level and hook to your s3 bucket.
[02:34] Priya: 90 days is fine but we need the deletion guarantee and audit trail for when records are deleted — need to show that to our auditors.
[02:43] Samira: understood. we can provide a deletion audit entry — event_type: data_deletion, with request_id and user who initiated. we'll add that to the sample.
[02:56] Jamal: also need to know about PII — do you scrub or mask prompt content in logs?
[03:05] Ethan: great q. our default is to keep prompt metadata but we can configure redaction. we do not persist full prompt text in the control-plane logs for Dedicated or Private if the customer requests, but for hosted pilot the streaming/serving logs include token counts and truncated prompts. i will clarify exact truncation rules. sometimes the transcript text shows partial prompt hashing.

[05:00] Nora: quick interjection — for product acceptance we need rerunable tests that show deleted data is irrecoverable. is that something you can support?
[05:08] Maya: yes our platform supports deletion workflows and we can run a sample deletion with you in a demo environment, we will capture the deletion event, then show the backup lifecycle.

[06:12] Ethan: moving to SSO — we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC. Most customers use Okta. The pilot tenant you gave us earlier should work. For SAML we'll exchange metadata XML and configure SP-initiated SSO. There is also SCIM for user provisioning.
[06:42] Priya: we use Okta and SCIM; user groups map to RBAC roles. Can we restrict who can call the model (i.e., per-route RBAC)?
[06:51] Ethan: yes you can tie groups to API access roles. We have route-level policies in the Console. caveat: the SE config for token-level cost tracking requires a service role with read for billing. We'll document minimal scopes.
[07:20] Luis: when you say 'route-level' do you mean per-route in the console or per-API-key? we want both ideally.
[07:27] Ethan: both — you can bind a key to a route and a group. For the pilot we usually do a scoped API key mapped to the SSO group.

[08:00] Priya: about key management — do you support customer-managed keys? we can't have all keys manged by a vendor key.
[08:08] Samira: for Private and Dedicated we support KMS integration (AWS KMS & CloudHSM for on-prem). For hosted we offer envelope encryption with our KMS but can integrate with customer KMS via Bring-Your-Own-Key for certain enterprise plans. For the pilot we can show a mock KMS key policy.
[08:34] Jamal: do you rotate keys automatically? what are the guarantees?
[08:38] Ethan: automatic rotation is supported on Dedicated and Private; hosted rotation is quarterly unless you opt into BYOK where you control rotation. We'll send the key-rotation SLA in the doc pack.

[10:10] Derek: i'm more concerned about network isolation — during the pilot we saw some telemetry hitting multiple regions, is that expected?
[10:18] Samira: probably routing fallback. For hosted we have smart routing that can go to nearest region; we can pin to a region for the pilot to avoid cross-region telemetry. We'll show routing logs.

[12:00] Ethan: back to audit logs — sample export: we'll give you a gzipped newline-delimited JSON for 30 days with a mapping csv to your SIEM fields. Keep in mind some fields may appear slightly different in early pilot builds.
[12:22] Priya: we run Splunk; the mapping csv helps but we also need an example of a deletion event and an account access event for a compliance report.
[12:30] Ethan: yep will include account.access.grant and data_deletion events.

[14:10] Luis: latency/trace data — do you include request_id that correlates across traces and logs?
[14:16] Ethan: yes request_id ties serving logs to control-plane, and we also emit trace_id. there's also a kv-cache hit flag that shows whether responses were served from cache which affects token counts. sometimes kv is transcribed as 'kayv' in our auto transcripts, apologies.

[16:00] Priya: SOC2 — what level of evidence can you give? we need to test control access, change management, incident response.
[16:10] Samira: we have a SOC2 Type II for our control plane — we'll share the summary and a redacted attestation. For the pilot-specific hosting configuration we'll provide a scoping doc that maps which controls apply to hosted vs dedicated vs private. That helps you show how the pilot environment is covered.
[16:36] Priya: is there a statement-of-applicability or gap doc?
[16:40] Maya: yes we'll provide a SOC2 scoping matrix and a short gap analysis for the pilot footprint. note that some controls require on-prem evidence for Private deployments.

[18:00] Derek: more practical question — if we ask for 30-day logs and immediate deletion after 30 days, what is the SLA to confirm deletion?
[18:08] Ethan: we normally provide a deletion confirmation event within 24 hours of the deletion job running; for the pilot we can produce a signed hash of the deletion job output as proof.
[18:20] Jamal: can you support retention shorter than 7 days? e.g., 72 hrs for a particular dataset?
[18:27] Samira: yes but with tradeoffs — shorter retention increases operational cost and may limit ability to debug. it's doable. we'll note the cost delta in our follow-up.

[20:00] Nora: product question — for evaluation we need a reproducible pipeline that strips PII before logs hit your control-plane. is there a webhook or pre-log hook?
[20:08] Ethan: you can run a preprocessor in your VPC that scrubs prompts and forwards non-PII events to our ingest endpoint; for Private/Dedicated we can deploy that as a sidecar. For hosted we offer a server-side redaction layer but with limited rule customization.

[22:00] Priya: can you show the sample retention policy config? field names and how to set retention by event_type?
[22:12] Ethan: we'll attach the retention config snippet — it uses a retention_policy map: event_type->days, plus default_retention. i'll make sure the snippet is compatible with your SIEM.

[24:10] Samira: quick status check on outstanding asks from last week — did you get the pilot traffic replay?
[24:18] Derek: yes we replayed a small corpus, saw some token count anomalies but nothing blocking.
[24:30] Ethan: that's the kv-cache behavior — when cache warms you see fewer tokens, which is expected. we'll show before/after charts.

[26:00] Priya: legal would like to see a sample DPA clause about data retention and deletion. Jamal, did you want us to re-run that with Redwood legal?
[26:10] Jamal: yes please. we'll need a DPA redline and a short memo on data jurisdiction during the pilot — we prefer logs to remain in us-east-1.
[26:20] Samira: ok we'll scope region pinning for the pilot.

[28:00] Ethan: brief note on encryption — data at rest is encrypted; we provide TLS for in-flight. For BYOK you put the master key in your KMS and we use envelope encryption. We'll include a sample key policy showing decrypt permissions only for the service role.

[30:00] Derek: what about incident response? if a data-exposure event occurs, what's the SR process and timelines?
[30:08] Maya: our incident playbook has 4-hour triage SLA, 24-hour initial report, and postmortem deliverable. For pilot customers we follow the same cadence. We can share a redacted IR template.

[33:10] Priya: i know some vendors provide a tamper-evident log storage option — do you offer something like WORM or append-only for audit logs?
[33:20] Ethan: currently we support write-once S3 lifecycle with MFA-delete option for Dedicated/Private. For hosted we can mount logs to a WORM-configured bucket on request for enterprise. i'll include notes.

[35:00] Nora: small question — do you surface per-token cost in the audit logs or just in console metrics?
[35:06] Ethan: both — we emit token count per request in the serving log and the console has aggregated token cost. the log has token_in, token_out, model_id. sometimes model names get mangled — e.g., 'redwood-m' might come through as 'rw-m' in older builds.

[37:30] Derek: any blockers from Redwood side to provide the sample artifacts and schedule the SSO test?
[37:38] Samira: no blockers — we already have the Okta metadata you uploaded. We'll send the docs and SSO test slots.

[38:00] Ethan: one more note on retention: if you request deletion of prompts that contain PII, we recommend an ingestion-side hash-index so you can prove the record was removed without keeping the full prompt in logs. we'll include a sample script.

[40:10] Priya: good. also would like a short one-page controls mapping for our auditors that maps Redwood controls to our internal control IDs.
[40:18] Maya: we'll create a one-pager and include the mapping — that's action for me.

[42:00] Samira: recap — we'll send: SOC2 summary + scoping matrix, 30-day audit-log sample (gz), retention config snippet, KMS key policy sample, SSO test slots, DPA draft for redline, and the one-page controls mapping. Ethan will attach the log examples and deletion event. Maya will add compliance pack.
[42:30] Derek: sounds good. can we get most of those items in the next 5 business days?
[42:36] Samira: yes we will target that.
[43:00] Priya: thanks all, that covers my main concerns.
[43:10] Jamal: ok let's reconvene after the SSO test and once we review the SOC2 materials.
[43:20] Samira: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the SSO test and the e2e log review.
[43:30] Ethan: thanks, bye.
[43:35] (end)

Notes on transcription quality: multiple acronyms awkwardly transcribed (KV cache -> 'kayv', SAML sometimes 'sam l'), occasional speaker label overlaps.

References shared: link: /pilot/artifacts/ORCH-42/soc2_summary.pdf (sent post-call), link: /pilot/artifacts/ORCH-42/auditlog_sample_30d.jsonl.gz, link: calendar invite: SSO-test-2025-11-06, DPA draft (docx).

Final recap (plain): Samira/Sales to send SOC2 and DPA draft; Ethan/SE to provide log sample + retention config + KMS policy; Maya to produce simplified control mapping and add to pilot folder; OrchidAI (Priya/Luis) to confirm retention window and run Okta test.
